exposure: Maternal age group (<30 years, 30-34 years, 35-37 years, 38-40 years)
cohort: The study included 1,279 women who underwent frozen-thawed high-quality single blastocyst transfer, divided into four age groups: <30 years, 30-34 years, 35-37 years, and 38-40 years.
finding: Women aged 35-37 years undergoing frozen-thawed high-quality single blastocyst transfer had comparable pregnancy outcomes to younger patients, while those aged 38-40 years experienced significantly lower clinical pregnancy and live birth rates and were at higher risk for non-live birth and adverse pregnancy outcomes.
followup_time: Up to neonatal outcomes (specific duration not mentioned)
